rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-minsaʾa is the large staff a shepherd uses to drive his flock, from nasʾ when he urges a she-camel or camel onward.
rows.anchor: والمنسأة العصا الكبيرة التي يسوق بها الراعي غنمه مفعلة من نسأت الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory, equivalent to “that is”; the implied wording is “We said: make complete coats of mail,” or it may mean “in order to make.” This an can precede a command.
rows.anchor: أن ها هنا في تأويل التفسير والقول وهي تدعي المفسرة بمعنى أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “measure” is omitted and understood as the rings and nails of the mail.
rows.anchor: وقدر مفعوله محذوف أي قدر الحلق والمسامير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The morning and evening journeys are accusative circumstantial clauses, with “a journey” omitted; the subjugation expressed in “for Solomon was the wind” governs them.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال والتقدير غدوها مسيرة شهر ورواحها كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And whoever works” is accusative under an understood “We subjected from among the jinn those who work.”
rows.anchor: ومن يعمل في موضع نصب على تقدير وسخرنا من الجن من يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shukran can be a cognate accusative, understood as “give thanks, thanking”; alternatively it is purpose, with “obedience” understood as the object of “do.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعول اعملوا على تقدير اشكروا شكرا كما تقول أحمد الله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli parses an as a reduced form of the emphatic particle: when Solomon fell, the jinn’s condition became clear, namely that they did not know the unseen; the clause substitutes for “the jinn.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: والتقدير فلما خر تبين أمر الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says tabayyana is intransitive here, as in the cited examples “it became clear to you” and “when it became clear to him.”
rows.anchor: ولفظ تبين هنا لازم غير متعد مثله في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon’s fall exposed the jinn’s ignorance of the unseen: the jinn never claimed such knowledge, but people believed they had it, and his death disproved that belief.
rows.anchor: فلما خر انكشف للإنس أمر الجن من جهلهم بالغيب وذلك لأن الجن ما ادعوا علم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning servants who turn back to God, the passage turns to David and Solomon; God favored David with prophethood, scripture, decisive judgment, and miracles.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر عباد الله المنيبين إليه وصله سبحانه بذكر داود وسليمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Mujahid say God commanded the mountains to praise with David whenever he praised God, and they did so.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد قالوا: أمر الله الجبال أن تسبح معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linguistic interpretation is “return the praise with him,” deriving awb from āba, yaʾūbu, to return.
rows.anchor: وتأويله عند أهل اللغة رجعي معه التسبيح من آب يؤوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God caused praise to issue from the mountains as a miracle for David; birds may also praise if God grants them discernment to understand it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون سبحانه فعل في الجبال ما يأتي به منها التسبيح معجزا له

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says the mountains traveled with David wherever he went as a miracle; taʾwib means traveling by day.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك معجزا له عن الجبائي والتأويب السير بالنهار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the mountains complied with David’s purposes, such as digging wells, finding springs or ore, and laying roads.
rows.anchor: معناه ارجعي إلى مراد داود فيما يريده من حفر بئر واستنباط عين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says iron became like wax in David’s hand, so he could shape it without fire or hammer.
rows.anchor: فصار في يده كالشمع يعمل به ما شاء من غير أن يدخله النار ولا أن يضربه بالمطرقة عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told David to make complete coats of mail from iron; He softened it and taught him the craft because David wanted to live by his own work.
rows.anchor: أي قلنا له اعمل من الحديد دروعا تامات وإنما ألان الله تعالى الحديد لداود لأنه أحب أن يأكل من كسب يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David was the first to make armor; he sold it, fed his family, and gave charity from the proceeds.
rows.anchor: وعلمه صنعة الدرع وكان أول من اتخذها وكان يبيعها ويأكل من ثمنها

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that God praised David but reproached him for eating from the public treasury; David wept forty mornings, then made 360 coats, selling them for 360,000 dirhams and becoming self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع قال: إن الله أوحى إلى داود ع نعم العبد أنت إلا أنك تأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabighat means complete, full-coverage coats of mail.
rows.anchor: أي قلنا له اعمل من الحديد دروعا تامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard is the interweaving of armor; its maker is called a sarrad or zarrad. Nails should be neither too thin, lest they split, nor too thick, lest they break the rings.
rows.anchor: أي عدل في نسج الدروع ومنه

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman watched David make his first coat in silence, then praised it as excellent war protection; he remarked that silence is wisdom, though few practice it.
rows.anchor: حكي أن لقمان حضر داود عند أول درع عملها فجعل يتفكر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told David and his household to perform righteous acts as thanks for His great blessings.
rows.anchor: أي وقلنا اعمل أنت وأهلك الصالحات وهي الطاعات شكرا لله سبحانه على عظيم نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what they do; none of their deeds is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: أي أنا عالم بما تفعلونه لا يخفى علي شيء من أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also subjected the wind to Solomon.
rows.anchor: أي وسخرنا لسليمان الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind covered a month’s journey morning and evening, a two-month journey in a day for a rider.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنها كانت تسير في اليوم مسيرة شهرين للراكب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Solomon traveled a month’s distance before noon and another month’s distance from noon to evening.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كان يغدو مسيرة شهر إلى نصف النهار ويروح مسيرة شهر إلى آخر النهار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan places the morning journey from Damascus to Ashtakhar in Isfahan and the evening journey from there to Kabul, each a month’s distance for a fast traveler; the wind carried Solomon and his troops.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كان يغدو من دمشق فيقيل باصطخر من أرض أصفهان وبينهما مسيرة شهر للمسرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Solomon the wind in place of his fine swift horses.
rows.anchor: أعطاه الله الريح بدلا من الصافنات الجياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harur is the hot wind called samum; al-Farraʾ distinguishes samum as daytime only, while harur occurs by day and night.
rows.anchor: الحرور السموم وهي الريح الحارة قال الفراء السموم لا يكون إلا بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwaʾ is one of two things attaining the same measure; in a road or piece of wood it also means straightness, opposite to crookedness.
rows.anchor: والاستواء حصول أحد الشيئين على مقدار الآخر ومنه الاستواء في العود والطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make someone hear is to bring about an audible sound in a form the hearer can perceive.
rows.anchor: والاسماع إيجاد المسموع بحيث يدركه السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s judgment is just: no soul bears another soul’s sin, and each is answerable for the wrong it commits.
rows.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل نفس أخرى أي لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره وإنما يؤاخذ كل بما يقترفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a soul weighed down by sins asks another to carry some of its burden, that other bears nothing, even if closely related.
rows.anchor: أي وأن تدع نفس مثقلة بالآثام غيرها الى أن يتحمل عنها شيئا من إثمها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas pictures a father or mother asking a child to carry a burden; the child replies that his own burden is enough.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يقول الأب والأم يا بني احمل عني فيقول حسبي ما علي

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who fear their Lord while absent from the judgments and terrors of the afterlife are the ones who benefit from warning; warning has no effect on others.
rows.anchor: أي وهم غائبون عن أحكام الآخرة وأهوالها وهذا كقوله إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they fear their Lord in private, away from other people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذين يخشون ربهم في خلواتهم وغيبتهم عن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They maintain prayer and observe its conditions.
rows.anchor: أداموها وقاموا بشرائطها وإنما عطف الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense for establishing prayer alongside the present tense for fearing signals that fear is constant whereas prayer has appointed times.
rows.anchor: وإنما عطف الماضي على المستقبل إشعارا باختلاف المعنى لأن الخشية لازمة في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakka means performing obedience and fulfilling zakat and other duties.
rows.anchor: أي فعل الطاعات وقام بما يجب عليه من الزكاة وغيرها من الواجبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is purification from sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تطهر من الأثام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefit and reward of purification return to the person who purifies himself, not someone else.
rows.anchor: لأن جزاء ذلك يصل إليه دون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures return to God, the sole judge, who rewards each according to his deeds.
rows.anchor: أي مرجع الخلق كلهم إلى حيث لا يملك الحكم إلا الله سبحانه فيجازي كلا على قدر عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind is one blind to the path of truth, while the sighted is guided by it.
rows.anchor: أي لا يتساوى الأعمى عن طريق الحق والذي اهتدى إليه قط

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading of the contrast is the polytheist and the believer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المشرك والمؤمن { ولا الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses represent polytheism and error, while the light represents faith and guidance.
rows.anchor: أي ظلمات الشرك والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added la has two analyses: it may reinforce the negation, or it may negate the equality of each item with its counterpart separately.
rows.anchor: وما بعده من زيادة لا قولان: أحدهما: أنها زائدة مؤكدة للنفي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets shade and hot wind as Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني الجنة والنار عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is shade at night and the scorching wind by day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني ظل الليل والسموم بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living and dead represent believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يعني المؤمنين والكافرين. وقيل: يعني العلماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is scholars and ignorant people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني العلماء والجهال وقال بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrasts can also be literal examples: just as these things differ and do not resemble each other, worship of God differs from worship of another, as do believer and unbeliever, truth and falsehood, and scholar and ignorant person.
rows.anchor: أراد نفس الأعمى والبصير والظل والحرور والظلمات والنور على طريق ضرب المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God benefits through hearing whomever He wills to favor and guide; this does not deny that unbelievers literally heard His signs.
rows.anchor: أي ينفع بالإسماع من يشاء أن يلطف له ويوفقه ولم يرد به نفي حقيقة السماع

words: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُسْمِعٍۢ مَّن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot make unbelievers benefit from hearing when they refuse to accept, just as the dead in graves cannot hear.
rows.anchor: أي إنك لا تقدر على أن تنفع الكفار بإسماعك إياهم إذ لم يقبلوا

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says judad are paths or lines; the singular is jadda, while the word is also the plural of jadid.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد الجدد الطرائق والخطوط

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse uses jadda for the dark stripe on a wild ass’s back.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: كأن سراته وجدة متنه كنائن

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains the mountain judad as paths like white, black, and red veins.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هي الطرائق تكون في الجبال كالعروق بيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharabib are intensely black, like the color of a crow.
rows.anchor: والغربيب الشديد السواد الذي يشبه لون الغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtalifan is an adjective of fruits, while “their colors differ” is a predicate of an omitted subject, understood as “it is diverse in color.”
rows.anchor: مختلفا صفة لثمرات وألوانها مرفوع بأنه فاعله مختلف ألوانه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “its colors” may refer to the understood subject or to a described kind; the author prefers the latter analysis, “a kind diverse in color.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الهاء عائدا إلى موصوف لمختلف تقدير جنس مختلف ألوانه وهو الأصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two words may be circumstantial accusatives, or adjectives describing the manner of giving; yarjūna is also circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: سرا وعلانية يجوز أن يكون نصبهما على الحال على تقدير أنفقوا مسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse returns to signs of divine oneness in the rain, plants, mountains, people, animals, and livestock.
rows.anchor: ثم عاد الكلام إلى ذكر دلائل التوحيد فقال سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person plural in “We brought forth” is a form of majestic and exalted speech.
rows.anchor: أخبر عن نفسه بنون الكبرياء والعظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits vary in color, taste, and smell; color is singled out because it is most apparent and implies the other qualities.
rows.anchor: وطعومها وروائحها اقتصر على ذكر الألوان لأنها أظهر ولدلالة الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain judad are white and red paths.
rows.anchor: أي طرق بيض وطرق حمر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes the wording as inverted order, meaning “black gharabib,” since Arabic says “black, intensely black.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وهذا على التقديم والتأخير تقديره وسود غرابيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects inversion: sud is explanatory apposition or, preferably, emphasis, since gharabib are necessarily black.
rows.anchor: وأقول: ينبغي أن يكون سود عطف بيان يبين غرابيب به

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَٰنُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People, land animals, and livestock—such as camels, sheep, and cattle—also have varied colors, like fruits and mountains.
rows.anchor: التي تدب على وجه الأرض

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only scholars who truly know God fear Him with proper fear and guard against His disobedience and punishment.
rows.anchor: أي ليس يخاف الله حق خوفه ولا يحذر معاصيه خوفا من نقمته إلا العلماء

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says scholars are those whose deeds confirm their words; whoever’s deeds fail to match his words is not a scholar.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: يعني بالعلماء من صدق قوله فعله

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says those among creation who fear God are those who know His might, grandeur, and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: يريد إنما يخافني من خلقي من علم جبروتي وعزتي

rows.speaker: زيد عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Zayd, transmitting from Yaʿqub, reads lamustaqirri with kasra on qaf; the remaining readers use a fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ زيد عن يعقوب لمستقر لها بكسر القاف والباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
rows.claim: Readers of the Hijaz and Basra, except Abu Jaʿfar and Ruways, read al-qamar in the nominative; the others read it in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة غير أبي جعفر ورويس والقمر بالرفع والباقون بالنصب

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين، أبو جعفر الباقر، جعفر الصادق، ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، عكرمة، عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: A reading transmitted from ʿAli b. al-Husayn, al-Baqir, al-Sadiq, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, ʿIkrima, and ʿAtaʾ has la mustaqirra laha with the ra in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن الحسين زين العابدين ع وأبي جعفر الباقر وجعفر الصادق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli explains nominative al-qamar as a new sign parallel to “the night is a sign”; the clauses that follow explain the sign, as an explanatory clause may explain a promise or instruction.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الرفع على تقدير

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On this nominative analysis, ayatun is an indefinite subject, lahum modifies it, and an understood predicate is “in sight” or “in existence.”
rows.anchor: والقول في آية أنه يرتفع بالابتداء ولهم صفة للنكرة والخبر مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading links the moon to an object-fronted construction such as “Zaydan I struck.”
rows.anchor: ومن نصب فقد حمله على زيدا ضربته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “it has no resting place” sounds unrestricted, it means no rest while the heavens remain as they are; when they vanish, the sun settles and its course ends.
rows.anchor: فظاهره العموم والمعنى الخصوص فهو بمنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited lament means “if I lived forever, I would keep mourning you,” illustrating the restricted sense of the sun’s lack of rest.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لو عشت أبدا لبكيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salakh means to remove a thing from its covering, like stripping an animal from its hide; 7:175 uses it for leaving something that once covered one.
rows.anchor: السلخ إخراج الشيء من لباسه ومنه إخراج الحيوان من جلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ʿurjun is the cluster bearing the date-palm’s branchlets, also called ʿuthkul, ʿithkal, kabasa, or qinw; the word is on the faʿlul pattern.
rows.anchor: والعرجون العذق الذي فيه الشماريخ وهو العثكول والعثكال والكباسة والقنو

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba’s verse uses muʿarjan in describing a graceful, curved form, cited for the word ʿurjun.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: في خدر مياس الدمى معرجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manazil is understood as “possessor of stations,” with the noun deleted and its genitive substitute promoted; the moon is not stations but moves through them.
rows.anchor: تقديره ذا منازل ثم حذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manazil cannot be a direct locative because it is bounded; a verb takes a bounded place through a preposition, as “I sat in the mosque,” not “I sat the mosque.”
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن ينصب منازل على الظرف لأنه محدود والفعل لا يصل إلى المحدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted and free of defect, deserving the utmost praise and gratitude, because He created pairs and kinds throughout creation.
rows.anchor: ثم نزه سبحانه نفسه وعظمها دالا بذلك على أنه هو الذي يستحق منتهى الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairs include male and female animals and kinds of date palms, grains, figs, and vines.
rows.anchor: أي تنزيها وتعظيما وبراءة عن السوء للذي خلق الأصناف والأشكال من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase includes all the plants the earth grows.
rows.anchor: مما تنبت الأرض } أي من سائر النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created from human beings offspring in pairs, male and female.
rows.anchor: أي وخلق منهم أولادا أزواجا ذكورا وإناثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unknown pairs include things in the depths of the earth and at the bottom of the seas, beyond human sight or report.
rows.anchor: مما في بطون الأرض وقعر البحار فلم يشاهدوه ولم يتصل خبره بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is another sign: God strips away sunlight, leaving the air dark as it was before, since the sun is what illuminates the air.
rows.anchor: أي ننزع منه ونخرج ضوء الشمس فيبقى الهواء مظلما كما كان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats night as a dark body and day as its peel: day is an incidental covering, while night is the underlying original.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال سبحانه { نسلخ منه النهار } لأنه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They enter night without light.
rows.anchor: أي داخلون في الليل لا ضياء لهم فيه

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: A group of commentators says the sun runs until its course ends at the end of the world; Abu Muslim says this is the same as having no rest until then.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها تجري لانتهاء أمرها عند انقضاء الدنيا فلا تزال تجري

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim equates the sun’s appointed course with having no resting place until the world ends.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: ومعنى هذا ومعنى لا مستقر لها واحد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the sun runs for a fixed period that it neither exceeds nor varies from.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أنها تجري لوقت واحد لا تعدوه ولا يختلف عن قتادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation is that the sun reaches its farthest stations in winter and summer, with limits to both its ascent and descent.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: أنها تجري إلى أقصى منازلها في الشتاء والصيف لا تتجاوزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty is the all-capable one whom nothing defeats; the Knowing is one from whom nothing is hidden.
rows.anchor: أي القادر الذي لا يعجزه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon has 28 stations, moving through one each day and night without variation until it traverses its orbit.
rows.anchor: وهي ثمانية وعشرون منزلا ينزل كل يوم وليلة منزلة منها لا يختلف حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At month’s end the moon becomes thin like an old, dry, curved date stalk, then disappears for two days; an old cluster dries and curves in the same way.
rows.anchor: أي عاد في آخر الشهر دقيقا كالعذق اليابس العتيق ثم يخفى يومين آخر الشهر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the date cluster takes this dry, curved form every six months.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن العذق يصير كذلك في كل ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: In a disputation with the Waqifi Abu Saʿid al-Makkari, al-Rida used the Jesus-Mary relation to explain his unity with his father, then ruled that ownership for six months counts as qadim in a deathbed manumission clause; Abu Saʿid later lost his sight and begged until death.
rows.anchor: دخل أبو سعيد المكاري وكان واقفيا على أبي الحسن الرضا ع فقال له أبلغ من قدرك

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida rules that “old” property in a deathbed declaration freeing all old slaves includes anyone the owner has possessed for six months.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: ما ملكه لستة أشهر فهو قديم وهو حر

words: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun does not catch the moon because it moves more slowly, taking a year to pass its stations while the moon takes a month; God maintains their separate revolutions and orbits.
rows.anchor: لأن الشمس أبطأ سيرا من القمر فإنها تقطع منازلها في سنة والقمر يقطعها في شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night does not get ahead of day.
rows.anchor: أي ولا يسبق الليل النهار

words: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْءَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What was revealed is a reminder and clear Qur’an from the Lord of the worlds, not poetry, rajaz, or a sermon.
rows.anchor: ليس بشعر ولا رجز ولا خطبة والمراد بالذكر أنه يتضمن ذكر الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a reminder because it contains rulings, proofs, and accounts of past nations; it is Qur’an because its parts are gathered together, so the two terms have distinct benefits.
rows.anchor: وبالقرآن أنه مجموع بعضه إلى بعض فجمع سبحانه بينهما لاختلاف فائدتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation warns those alive in faith against disobeying God; an unbeliever is like the dead, or worse, since he gains no benefit from his religion and is harmed by it.
rows.anchor: أي أنزلناه لتخوف به من معاصي الله من كان مؤمنا لأن الكافر كالميت

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Another explanation transmitted from ʿAli is that the living person is one with reason.
rows.anchor: المراد بمن كان حيا عاقلا وروي ذلك عن علي ع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says “alive” means alive in heart and sight.
rows.anchor: حي القلب حي البصر عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat and punishment become due upon unbelievers because of their unbelief.
rows.anchor: أي يجب الوعيد والعذاب على الكافرين بكفرهم

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads wa-yazidun with an initial waw; al-Tabrisi says the rationale is evident.
rows.anchor: قرأ جعفر بن محمد الصادق ع ويزيدون بالواو والوجه فيه ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghabir is what remains briefly after the rest has passed; ghubar (dust) is so named because a little remains after the dust has gone.
rows.anchor: الغابر الباقي قليلا بعد ما مضى ومنه الغبار لأنه يبقى بعد ذهاب التراب قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadmir is destruction meant as a punitive example.
rows.anchor: والتدمير الإهلاك على وجه التنكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An abiq is a fugitive who has gone where his pursuer cannot find him.
rows.anchor: والآبق الفار إلى حيث لا يهتدي إليه طالبه وقد أبق يابق إباقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashhun means full or loaded.
rows.anchor: والمشحون المملوء والمساهمة المقارعة مأخوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musahama is drawing lots, from casting arrows.
rows.anchor: والمساهمة المقارعة مأخوذ من إلقاء السهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahadat means an argument failed; the root is slipping, since one who passes over a slippery place falls.
rows.anchor: ودحضت حجته أي سقطت وأدحضها الله مأخوذ من الدحض وهو الزلق

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The quoted line “and he swerved as a camel swerves from a slippery place” illustrates dahd as a slippery surface; the poet is unnamed.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: وحاد كما حاد البعير عن الدحض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltqama means to swallow like a morsel; laqimahu, iltaqamahu, and talaqqamahu have the same sense.
rows.anchor: والالتقام ابتلاع اللقمة يقال: لقمه والتقمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is mulim when he has done something blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وألام الرجل فهو مليم أتى بما يلام عليه

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s verse uses ghayr mulim, “not blameworthy,” to illustrate the word.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: سفها عذلت ولمت غير مليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaraʾ is open ground without trees or other cover; it can also mean an empty face of the earth.
rows.anchor: والعراء الفضاء الذي لا يواريه شجر ولا غيره

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The verse about casting clothes down in the open country illustrates al-ʿaraʾ as bare ground; the poet is unnamed.
rows.anchor: قال: ورفعت رجلا لا أخاف عثارها ونبذت بالبلد العراء ثيابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqtin is any plant that survives from winter into summer without a trunk.
rows.anchor: واليقطين كل شجرة تبقى من الشتاء إلى الصيف ليس لها ساق

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: Umayya b. Abi al-Salt’s verse describes a gourd grown through God’s mercy, cited for yaqtin.
rows.anchor: قال أمية بن أبي الصلت: فأنبت يقطينا عليه برحمة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqtin follows the yafʿil pattern from qatana, to reside temporarily; qutani are household-stored legumes such as chickpeas, lentils, and vinegar, with singulars qitniyya and qatina.
rows.anchor: وهو يفعيل من قطن بالمكان إذا أقام به إقامة زائل لا إقامة راسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musbihin is a circumstantial accusative with tamurrun; the prepositional phrase bil-layl is also accusative in coordination with it.
rows.anchor: بالليل الجار والمجرور أيضا في موضع نصب عطفا عليه تقديره لتمرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot was one of God’s messengers, sent to call his people to obedience and affirm divine oneness.
rows.anchor: أي رسولا من جملة من أرسله الله إلى خلقه داعيا لهم إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is attached to an omitted command: “remember when We saved him,” meaning God rescued Lot and his believers from the annihilating punishment.
rows.anchor: إذ يتعلق بمحذوف وكأنه قيل أذكر يا محمد إذ نجيناه أي خلصناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s wife is excepted from his people and remained among those destroyed.
rows.anchor: استثنى من جملة قومه امرأته فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the rest of Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: أي أهلكناهم { وإنكم لتمرون عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Arab polytheists: on their travels to and from Syria, they pass Lot’s towns by day and night; they should reflect and avoid the disbelief and error that ruined its people.
rows.anchor: هذا خطاب لمشركي العرب أي تمرون في ذهابكم ومجيئكم إلى الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeatedly passing sites of warning makes a person more culpable than rarely seeing them; prophetic stories encourage noble conduct and turn people away from unbelievers’ vices.
rows.anchor: ومن كثر مروره بموضع العبر كان ألوم ممن قل ذلك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah was one of the messengers; he fled from his people to a crowded ship, fearing punishment would fall on them while he remained among them.
rows.anchor: أي فر من قومه إلى السفينة المملوءة من الناس والأحمال خوفا من أن ينزل العذاب بهم

rows.speaker: الحسن، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn ʿAbbas say Jonah drew lots with the people and was among those who lost.
rows.anchor: أي من المقروعين عن الحسن وابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the outcome as being among those selected by lot to be thrown into the sea.
rows.anchor: من المسهومين عن مجاهد والمراد من الملقين في البحر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the ship faced sinking, so the people thought that throwing one passenger overboard would save the rest.
rows.anchor: واختلف في سبب ذلك فقيل: إنهم أشرفوا على الغرق فرأوا أنهم إن طرحوا واحدا منهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the ship stopped because a runaway slave was aboard; the sailors drew lots three times, each time selecting Jonah, so they recognized him as the fugitive and he threw himself into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن السفينة احتبست فقال الملاحون إن ها هنا عبدا آبقا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third account says the crew threw Jonah into the sea after the lot fell to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما وقعت القرعة عليه ألقوه في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish swallowed Jonah.
rows.anchor: أي ابتلعه. وقيل: إن الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told the whale Jonah was not made its food but its guest, and forbade it to break a bone or scratch his skin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله سبحانه أوحى إلى الحوت أني لم أجعل عبدي رزقا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah deserved blame as admonition, not punishment, for leaving his people without his Lord’s command.
rows.anchor: أي مستحق للوم لوم العتاب لا لوم العقاب على خروجه من بين قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s position is that Jonah only left a recommended act; a person can be blamed for neglecting a recommendation.
rows.anchor: وعندنا أن ذلك إنما وقع منه تركا للمندوب وقد يلام الإنسان على ترك المندوب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Those who allow minor sins for prophets say Jonah committed a minor sin that was expiated.
rows.anchor: ومن جوز الصغيرة على الأنبياء قال: قد وقع ذلك صغيرة مكفرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil b. Hayyan says Jonah remained in the whale for three days.
rows.anchor: كانت ثلاثة أيام عن مقاتل بن حيان

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAtaʾ says Jonah remained in the whale for seven days.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سبعة أيام عن عطاء

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah remained in the whale for twenty days.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عشرين يوما عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: السدي، مقاتل بن سليمان، الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, Muqatil b. Sulayman, and al-Kalbi say Jonah remained in the whale for forty days.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أربعين يوما عن السدي ومقاتل بن سليمان والكلبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Jonah had prayed in times of ease, so God rescued him in hardship.
rows.anchor: أي كان من المصلين في حال الرخاء فنجاه الله عند البلاء عن قتادة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr identifies Jonah’s praise as his prayer, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير. وقيل: من المسبحين أي من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may also mean those who declare God free of what is unfitting to His nature and remember Him.
rows.anchor: من المسبحين أي من المنزهين لله عما لا يليق به ولا يجوز في صفته

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without his being among those who praised God, Jonah’s belly in the whale would have become his grave until the resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي لصار بطن الحوت قبرا له إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cast Jonah onto bare ground without vegetation or trees; the whale was inspired to expel him onto the earth.
rows.anchor: أي فطرحناه بالمكان الخالي الذي لا نبت فيه ولا شجر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the bare place was the shore, where God inspired the whale to spit Jonah out.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالساحل ألهم الله سبحانه الحوت حتى قذفه ورماه من جوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah was sick when the whale expelled him.
rows.anchor: أي مريض حين ألقاه الحوت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the plant as a gourd.
rows.anchor: وهو القرع عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan say yaqtin is any plant that spreads over the ground and has no trunk.
rows.anchor: كل نبت يبسط على وجه الأرض ولا ساق له عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Jonah emerged from the whale like a fledgling without feathers and shaded himself under the plant from the sun.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود قال خرج يونس من بطن الحوت كهيئة فرخ ليس عليه ريش

words: وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the people as the inhabitants of Nineveh in the land of Mosul; Ibn ʿAbbas says the mission came after the whale expelled Jonah.
rows.anchor: قيل إن لله سبحانه أرسله إلى أهل نينوى من أرض الموصل في قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this chronology, Jonah could have been sent to a different people, or to his first people under a revealed law, after which they believed.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يجوز أن يكون أرسل إلى قوم بعد قوم ويجوز أن يكون أرسل إلى الأولين بشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first proposed explanation of “or” is deliberate ambiguity for the hearers: it is as if the verse said that Jonah was sent to one of the two numbers.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنه على طريق الإبهام على المخاطبين
